name: Hells Canyon of the Snake River
reach: Hells Canyon Dam to Heller Bar
agency: Hells Canyon National Recreation Area, Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
note: The deepest river canyon in North America. The 32-mile Wild section from the dam to Pittsburg Landing holds the big rapids and usually takes 3 to 4 days; the river continues about 48 miles to Heller Bar. Miles are from the Hells Canyon launch as in one mile-by-mile guide. The Snake is dam-controlled, with trip-reported flows of about 8,500 to 20,000 cfs. Camp sizes are from that guide; quality is not rated. Compiled from public sources; verify with the Forest Service and the USFS Boater's Guide.

rapids.name: Cliff Mountain Rapids
rapids.desc: Easy and visible from the put-in. Keep off the right-side rock face.

rapids.name: Brush Creek Rapids
rapids.desc: A read-and-run wave train.

rapids.name: Rocky Point Rapids
rapids.desc: Run best left of center.

rapids.name: Wild Sheep Rapid
rapids.desc: The longest rapid on the river, with big waves; the line changes with flow. Scout from river left at the creek confluence.

rapids.name: Granite Rapid
rapids.desc: A large submerged rock. The standard line is left under 20,000 cfs; the "Green Room" line opens around 19,000 cfs and up and few boats get through it without flipping. Scout river right just below Lower Granite Creek camp.

rapids.name: Three Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: A read-and-run wave train. Rated II+ by American Whitewater.

rapids.name: Upper Bernard Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Short; the weakness is usually on the left.

rapids.name: Lower Bernard Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Longer, with a large standing wave in the lower half. Great surfing for kayakers.

rapids.name: Waterspout Rapid
rapids.desc: A rock creates a hole at some flows and a sleeper hole on the lower left. At low water run from center left and drive hard right before the bottom. Washes out at high water. The river-right scout trail is shorter. Rated III+ by American Whitewater.

rapids.name: Bills Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: A read-and-run wave train.

rapids.name: Sluice Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Roller-coaster waves; a clear wave train down the right. Rated II by American Whitewater.

rapids.name: Rush Creek Rapids
rapids.desc: A large mid-river rock at the top can form a boat-sized hydraulic. A clear wave train runs down the right; more technical at low water. Rated III+ by American Whitewater.

history: Hells Canyon averages about 5,500 feet below the rim for roughly 75 miles, with the Seven Devils Mountains on the Idaho side. The dam complex upstream was built between 1959 and 1967.
In 1887 a group of Chinese miners was killed on the Oregon side. A memorial was erected in 2012.
In 1877 the Nez Perce crossed the Snake near Dug Bar during spring flood.
The river was designated Wild and Scenic in 1975. A 1954 proposal for a dam at Pleasant Valley was blocked by that protection.
flows: Releases are controlled at the dam. Granite Rapid was "juicing" near 20,000 cfs and ran fine at 14,000 to 15,000. Waterspout has options above 14,000 cfs. Check Idaho Power's flow line at 800-422-3143.

rules.d: At least one U.S. Coast Guard approved life jacket per person.
A reusable, sealable, leak-proof human waste carry-out system.
A fire pan for all fires.
An Oregon or Idaho invasive species sticker.
Respect pictographs and pit house sites; do not touch pictographs.
Treat all water before drinking. Pittsburg Landing has a spigot only in summer.
Rattlesnakes are present, including at the Suicide Point and Waterspout scout trails. Watch for poison ivy too.
Jet boats share the river and trip reports describe heavy traffic. Hold your line, and pull aside only as needed.
The Imnaha mine tunnel is gated to protect Townsend's big-eared bats.

permit.status: Required May 22 to Sept 10 (2026) · lottery for the Wild section

items.d: From the Friday before Memorial Day through September 10 (May 22 to September 10 in 2026), a Wild River Reservation is required seven days a week for the Wild section: Hells Canyon Dam to Upper Pittsburg Landing. Reservations are available only through Recreation.gov (877-444-6777).
Hells Canyon is part of the Four Rivers Lottery, with applications due January 31. Cancellations can be picked up on Recreation.gov. Confirm the current dates there.

Outside the primary season, and Monday through Thursday in the primary season, a self-issue permit is required for the whole corridor. No advance reservation is needed. Boat tags and permits come from the Clarkston, Washington Snake River office or a launch officer at Pittsburg Landing.

The permit holder must be at least 18, must not be under a late-cancellation or no-show penalty on this river, must sign a statement that they understand the definition of a private float boat trip, and cannot transfer the permit.
Three private permit launches are available daily in the primary season. Scenic floats launching from Pittsburg are limited to two a day on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and holidays.
A $6 reservation fee, non-refundable, paid by card on Recreation.gov. There are no per-person recreation fees.

Cancel on Recreation.gov no later than 15 days before launch. The deadline may be waived for extreme water conditions, but you must still cancel. A missed deadline is a no-show and affects permit eligibility for one year.

Powerboats are prohibited in the Wild section from the top of Wild Sheep Rapids to Kirkwood Upper Landing during non-motorized periods. These fall on Monday through Wednesday, beginning the first Monday in June and continuing every other week through the primary season.
Operating a kicker motor in the Wild section, from the Hells Canyon launch to Upper Pittsburg Landing, is prohibited except in an emergency.
